excerpt: There was a PR that went unreviewed and got closed, was that an omission? What's the way forward here? Personally I find it a corner case to first delete _default, but yea, should not break things. Could make _default impossible to delete as an alternative?

I believe there was no consensus how to address this issue. I would choose the following API behavior: - If the user omits the `baseConfigset` field in the request (null or not set), the configset is created without a base configset (no clone by default) - Is this possible? Can someone create a configset without a base structure? - The user has to set explicitly the `baseConfigset` to `_default` if they want to use…

Depends on when you want to land this change. If you require explicit baseConfigset param then that is back-compat-break and cannot land before 11.0. But falling back to _default and making it a protected configset would be back compat.
